root.name: Modern Defense: Anti-Modern
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c6 4. Bc4 d6 5. Qe2

overview: White sets up Bc4 and Qe2 against the Modern with e4+d4 and Nc3, eyeing f7 and keeping Nf3 and Be3 in reserve. Black has ...c6 and ...d6 behind a fianchettoed bishop and usually plays ...Nf6 or ...b5 to challenge the bishop, accepting less space for later counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Build e4+d4 with Nf3, Be3 and castling, using Qe2 to cover e4
Meet ...b5 with Bb3 and keep the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Undermine the centre with ...Nf6 and ...e5 or ...c5
Gain time against Bc4 with ...b5 or ...Nf6 then ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: White e4+d4 centre against Black c6, d6, Bg7 set-up

character.notes: Black is passive but safe and White has no immediate tactics; play is manoeuvring around the e4+d4 centre.

soundness.notes: Normal developing moves for both sides; neither is under threat.

structure.notes: Tension in the centre: White holds e4+d4, Black will challenge with ...e5 or ...c5, so it is not locked or open.

approach.notes: An anti-Modern line within the Modern complex, a standard sideline rather than a universal set-up.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the Modern needs good timing of the ...e5 or ...c5 break; little forced theory.

character.reason: Slow set-up with a clear centre for White but no forcing lines.

structure.reason: The e4+d4 centre is challenged later by ...e5 or ...c5.

approach.reason: A named anti-Modern line, respectable but not universal.

plans.reason: Black attacks the white centre from the wings with a fianchetto.
